title: A mine-cavity study found that geometric prediction accuracy varied by ground history
summary: On held-out cavity scans from one mine, a 3D U-Net achieved a mean overlap score of 0.601 versus 0.491 for the planning baseline. The ranking reversed in previously unexcavated ground: 0.525 for the learned model versus 0.592 for the baseline.

evidence.tested: The study randomly held out historical cavities and compared volume overlap against surveyed boundaries and the site’s geometric baseline.
evidence.unknown: The data came from one mine and roughly 90% of training-domain examples involved neighboring filled excavations. The subgroup scores do not establish prospective or cross-site reliability.
evidence.ai_role: The U-Net ensemble used recorded field inputs to estimate cavity geometry. Its predictions were compared with recorded cavity scans.
